summary.text: 到 means “arrive” or “reach.” Its usual analysis combines 至, which contributes that meaning, with 刀, which cues a related sound. A competing account of an older form remains unresolved.

formation.text: The usual analysis is phonosemantic: 至 contributes the meaning “arrive/reach,” and 刀 supplies a sound cue. In Baxter–Sagart’s Old Chinese system, 刀 *C.tˤaw and 到 *tˤaw[k]-s have related syllable shapes, though their reconstructed morphology and tone categories differ. A competing account reads an older seal-script form as 人 + 至, with 人 reinterpreted as 刀; the graphic transition and its chronology remain unresolved.

components.text: In the usual analysis, 至 contributes the meaning “arrive/reach.” It is a meaning-bearing part, not evidence that the whole character depicts a scene.
In the usual analysis, 刀 is the phonetic component. The sound comparison concerns the words’ pronunciation, not the name or pronunciation of an object depicted by 刀.

sound_limitation.text: The current Mandarin pair 刀 dāo and 到 dào is a modern comparison only; it does not establish their historical phonetic relationship.

sound.text: Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese reconstructions give 刀 and 到 related syllable shapes, though their reconstructed suffixes and tone categories differ.
Modern Mandarin readings 刀 dāo and 到 dào have similar syllable shapes, with different tones.

history.text: The Shuowen-era analysis divides 到 into 至 and phonetic 刀. A competing account interprets an older seal-script form as 人 + 至, with 人 reinterpreted as 刀. The transition, its chronology, and whether it involved graphic corruption remain unresolved. Databases list bronze, Warring States, seal, clerical, and regular-script forms, but their descriptions do not settle the competing analyses.

uncertainties.text: The earliest securely dated inscription and whether 到 occurs in oracle-bone records remain unresolved. A received 詩經 example supports an early literary use, but does not date the poem’s composition or transmission.
Other recorded senses include “go to,” “thorough/careful,” “deceive,” and “say/state.” Their chronology and semantic connections to “arrive/reach” are unresolved.

senses.text: The received 詩經·韓奕 phrase 靡國不到 is cited with the sense “reach/arrive.” It supports an early literary use, but does not date the poem’s composition or transmission.

limitations.text: The recorded senses beyond “arrive/reach” are not connected here because their chronology and semantic pathways are unresolved.
Reconstructions compare the sounds of 刀 and 到, but do not establish the historical name or pronunciation of any object depicted by 刀. No borrowing of 到 from an object-name is proposed.
